subject: biology
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 80 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); long answers 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The part of a bacterial cell where DNA lies is the ______. (b) The extra ring of DNA is called a ______.
Give the number of ATP molecules formed per glucose in (a) aerobic respiration (b) anaerobic respiration.
State true or false: (a) Arteries have valves. (b) Pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood.
State true or false: (a) The sympathetic system slows the heart. (b) Rods are sensitive to dim light.
Label the parts of the androecium and gynoecium (any one).
questions.answer: Androecium: anther (with pollen sacs), connective and filament. Gynoecium: stigma, style and ovary (with ovules).

questions.q: In a section of the ovary, identify the two structures A (large fluid-filled follicle with the ovum) and B (the yellowish body left after ovulation).
questions.answer: A: Graafian follicle. B: corpus luteum.

questions.q: Name the types of sex determination: (a) humans (b) birds.
Given the structure of DNA, fill in the blanks (any two): (a) the sugar is ______ (b) A pairs with ______ by ______ hydrogen bonds.

With reference to biological interactions between two species, identify the two wrong statements: (a) One organism benefits while the other is harmed: parasitism. (b) Both species cannot survive without the other: mutualism. (c) Penicillium secretes antibiotics which inhibit bacteria: predation. (d) One species benefits and the other is unharmed: commensalism.
questions.answer: (b) and (c) are wrong: (b) interdependence with neither able to survive is symbiosis (obligate mutualism); (c) Penicillium inhibiting bacteria is amensalism, not predation.

questions.q: Name the two forms of PEM.
Name two primary and two secondary lymphoid organs.
questions.answer: Primary: thymus and bone marrow; secondary: spleen and lymph nodes.

questions.q: Name the source to extract the following antibiotics: (a) Tetracycline (b) Streptomycin.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Distinguish between hormones and pheromones.
questions.answer: Hormones act inside the body of the same organism through blood; pheromones are released outside to influence other individuals of the same species.

questions.q: Write the functions of synergids and antipodal cells.
questions.answer: Synergids guide the pollen tube to the egg; antipodals degenerate and provide nutrition to the young embryo.

questions.q: Name two permanent surgical methods of birth control.
questions.answer: Vasectomy in males and tubectomy in females.

questions.q: Write two features of Down's syndrome.
questions.answer: Trisomy 21 (47 chromosomes), mental retardation and a thick tongue with a drooping face.

questions.q: Draw the diagram to show the structure of the DNA molecule.
questions.answer: Two antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbones coiled in a double helix with base pairs A=T (two hydrogen bonds) and G≡C (three hydrogen bonds) as rungs; one turn 3.4 nm contains 10 base pairs; diameter 2 nm.

questions.q: What are decomposers? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Organisms that feed on dead organic matter and recycle nutrients; bacteria and fungi.

questions.q: Write the deficiency diseases of vitamin A and vitamin D.
questions.answer: Vitamin A: night blindness and xerophthalmia. Vitamin D: rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

questions.q: What are memory cells?
questions.answer: B-cells that do not become plasma cells and remain to produce antibodies quickly if the antigen appears again.

questions.q: Write two drawbacks of antibiotics.
questions.answer: Bacteria become resistant by mutation, and antibiotics may kill useful gut bacteria or cause allergy.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the main features of the family Fabaceae.
questions.answer: Zygomorphic, bisexual flowers; five sepals; five papilionaceous petals (standard, two wings and two keel petals); ten diadelphous stamens; monocarpellary superior ovary with marginal placentation; the fruit is a pod; examples are pea and gram.

questions.q: Explain the types of placentation with one example each.
questions.answer: Marginal (pea), axile (china rose), parietal (mustard), basal (sunflower) and free central (Dianthus).

questions.q: Describe the characteristics of the genetic code.
questions.answer: Triplet, unambiguous, non-overlapping and commaless, degenerate (wobble), universal; AUG starts and UAA, UAG, UGA stop.

questions.q: Explain the structure of an antibody.
questions.answer: A Y-shaped immunoglobulin with two heavy and two light chains joined by disulphide bonds; the stem (Fc) is constant while the two prongs have variable antigen-binding sites.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the types of meristematic tissue with their location and function.
questions.answer: Apical meristem: root and shoot tips; increases length. Intercalary meristem: at the bases of leaves or internodes; increases internode length. Lateral meristem: cambium and cork cambium; increases thickness (secondary growth).

questions.q: Explain gene therapy and the single-gene disorders it may treat.
questions.answer: Replacement of the defective gene with a normal gene; SCID, haemophilia, sickle-cell anaemia and phenylketonuria.
